item.text:
**Reused evidence**
- None materially reused from the prior chapter cache for `6B`. The useful material here came from a different source set: Russian executive/legislative records, Rosstat, IMF, World Bank, UNICEF, the Bank of Russia, and Reuters.

**New evidence**
1. `N1` `Government meeting on implementation of the Presidential Executive Order on measures to support large families` — Government of Russia, 25 Jan 2024: [https://government.ru/en/news/50700/](https://government.ru/en/news/50700/). Claim: the government said 2024 was the Year of the Family by presidential decision and that parents with three or more children would receive equal support nationwide, regardless of region. Locator/excerpt: government meeting page, opening paragraphs. Type/credibility: official executive record; strong for what was decided, weaker for effect. Temporal fit: direct 2024 action. Attribution/limits: attributable to Putin’s presidency and agenda-setting, but implementation is shared with the cabinet and regions. Contrary points: does not prove broad welfare gains; it is a policy commitment. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.7`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

2. `N2` `Federal Law on an annual family payment for citizens with two or more children` — Government of Russia, 13 Jul 2024: [https://government.ru/docs/all/154255/](https://government.ru/docs/all/154255/). Claim: created a yearly means-tested family payment for working parents with two or more children, with eligibility tied to household income below 1.5 times the regional subsistence minimum. Type/credibility: primary legal record; strong for policy design. Temporal fit: enacted in 2024. Attribution/limits: executive/legislative act under the Putin system; effect depends on uptake and administration. Contrary points: targeted transfer, not universal service improvement. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

3. `N3` `Order establishing a unified certificate for large families` — Government of Russia, 29 Jun 2024: [https://government.ru/docs/all/154128/](https://government.ru/docs/all/154128/). Claim: created a nationwide standard certificate for large families and required regions to align issuance and digital confirmation. Type/credibility: official implementing order; strong for administrative rollout. Temporal fit: 2024. Attribution/limits: shows bureaucratic follow-through on the family policy package, but not outcome quality. Contrary points: mostly administrative harmonization. Lenses: `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.7`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

4. `N4` `Government to extend maternity capital through 2030` — Government of Russia, 18 Dec 2024: [https://government.ru/news/53768/](https://government.ru/news/53768/). Claim: the cabinet said, on the President’s initiative, the maternity-capital program would be extended to 2030 and could be used for housing, children’s education, and related family goals. Type/credibility: official policy announcement; strong for continuity and intent. Temporal fit: late-2024 policy decision. Attribution/limits: directly reflects presidential priority, but the measure predated 2024 and is cumulative. Contrary points: the page is descriptive of the mechanism, not independent proof of improved outcomes. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

5. `N5` `Government indexes social pensions by 7.5%` — Government of Russia, 7 Mar 2024: [https://government.ru/news/51065/](https://government.ru/news/51065/). Claim: social pensions were indexed by 7.5% from 1 April 2024, aimed at people without enough work history for an insurance pension. Type/credibility: official policy action; strong for transfer design. Temporal fit: direct 2024 action. Attribution/limits: relevant to vulnerable groups and older people, but the page itself does not measure adequacy versus inflation. Contrary points: single indexation step, not a full welfare assessment. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

6. `N6` `Additional funding for medical workers in rural areas` — Government of Russia, 18 Dec 2024: [https://government.ru/docs/53769/](https://government.ru/docs/53769/). Claim: the government approved extra funding to support medical workers in rural localities. Type/credibility: official budget/allocation record; strong for intent and allocation. Temporal fit: 2024. Attribution/limits: suggests a rural-health priority, but the page is allocation-level evidence, not delivery evidence. Contrary points: no direct evidence here of improved rural access or reduced waiting times. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`.

7. `N7` `Annual report on education policy in 2024` — Government of Russia, 21 May 2025: [https://government.ru/dep_news/55083/](https://government.ru/dep_news/55083/). Claim: the report says that at the start of 2024/25, about 18 million students were enrolled in general education, preschool access reached 99.8% by 1 Jan 2025, and third-shift schooling had been eliminated; it also says over 1,018,500 new school places were created since 2019 and major school renovation continued. Type/credibility: official annual sector report; good for service coverage, weaker for independent validation. Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 report. Attribution/limits: reflects national policy implementation under Putin’s administration, but many gains are multi-year and not uniquely 2024. Contrary points: quality outcomes, rural differences, and learning results are not fully captured. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

8. `N8` `Ministry of Health annual collegium on 2024 results` — Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation, 16 May 2025: [https://minzdrav.gov.ru/news/2025/05/16/25211-itogovaya-kollegiya-2024-i-plany-na-2025-klyuchevaya-zadacha-sistemy-zdravoohraneniya-sohranit-zhizni-i-zdorovie-grazhdan](https://minzdrav.gov.ru/news/2025/05/16/25211-itogovaya-kollegiya-2024-i-plany-na-2025-klyuchevaya-zadacha-sistemy-zdravoohraneniya-sohranit-zhizni-i-zdorovie-grazhdan). Claim: the ministry said 2024 work focused on higher life expectancy, lower mortality, national-project delivery, and better access to pediatric care; it also tied successes to new hospitals, equipment, and trained staff. Locator/excerpt: lines 97-100, 108-112, 134-148 on the open page. Type/credibility: official sector review; strong for government priorities, moderate for outcomes because it is self-assessment. Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 report. Attribution/limits: indicates executive priority and system activity, but the strongest outcome claims need independent corroboration. Contrary points: this is not an independent audit and does not establish nationwide equity. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

9. `N9` `Rosstat: poverty fell in Q1 2024` — Rosstat, 7 Jun 2024: [https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/238606](https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/238606). Claim: Rosstat said the share below the poverty line in Q1 2024 was 9.6%, down 2.5 points year over year; real incomes rose 5.9%, real disposable incomes 5.8%, the minimum wage rose 18.5%, and the lowest-income groups saw nominal income growth. Type/credibility: official statistics; strong for reported outcomes, but still subject to state-statistical caveats. Temporal fit: direct 2024 data. Attribution/limits: these are economy-wide outcomes under Putin’s 2024 government, but they reflect wages, prices, transfers, and broader macro conditions as well as policy. Contrary points: inflation was 7.61% in the quarter, so gains were not clean welfare gains. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

10. `N10` `Rosstat: poverty fell in Q3 2024` — Rosstat, 2024 update published 2024-11-? (search result page): [https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/250335](https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/250335). Claim: Rosstat reported poverty at 8.0% in Q3 2024, down 1.4 points year over year; real incomes rose 8.5% and real disposable incomes 9.4%, with the decline attributed to wage growth, targeted social programs, and social benefits. Type/credibility: official statistics. Temporal fit: direct 2024 quarter data. Attribution/limits: good for short-run household improvement, but still a mix of policy and war-economy effects. Contrary points: quarter-level improvement does not establish durable institutional gains. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

11. `N11` `Rosstat: full-year 2024 poverty, incomes, pensions, and inequality` — Rosstat, 12 Mar 2025: [https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/256247](https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/256247). Claim: Rosstat said 2024 poverty fell to 7.2%; in Q4 real incomes rose 8.6% and real disposable incomes 4.1%; social payments totaled 5.7 trillion rubles in Q4 and were up 10.9% year over year; average monthly nominal wages rose 18.8% nominally and 9.0% in real terms; the average pension rose 7.4%. Type/credibility: official annual statistical release. Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 full-year outcome. Attribution/limits: strong outcome evidence, but some gains are inflation-adjusted and partly driven by labor shortages and war spending. Contrary points: this does not tell us much about service quality, regional equality, or sustainability. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

12. `N12` `Rosstat: income differentiation in 2024` — Rosstat, 16 May 2025: [https://rosstat.gov.ru/statcurrentevents/document/260087](https://rosstat.gov.ru/statcurrentevents/document/260087). Claim: 2024 income concentration worsened slightly, with Gini at 0.379 and the richest quintile taking 44.3% of income; the poorest quintile received 6.1%. Type/credibility: official statistics; strong for inequality structure. Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 data. Attribution/limits: shows distributional limits even where poverty fell. Contrary points: this is evidence against broad-based fairness. Lenses: `6B.3`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`.

13. `N13` `World Bank country data: Russia` — World Bank, accessed 2026 page showing 2024 values: [https://data.worldbank.org/country/RU](https://data.worldbank.org/country/RU). Claim: life expectancy at birth was 73 in 2024; poverty at $3/day was 0.1 in 2023; population growth was negative. Locator/excerpt: lines 81-90 on the open page. Type/credibility: multilateral data portal; high credibility for the indicator values, though it is not ruler-specific. Temporal fit: 2024 life-expectancy value. Attribution/limits: this is outcome context, not direct proof of 2024 policy effectiveness. Contrary points: no direct causal attribution to Putin without supplementary evidence. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`.

14. `N14` `UNICEF country data: Russia` — UNICEF DATA, accessed 2026 page showing 2024 values: [https://data.unicef.org/country/rus/](https://data.unicef.org/country/rus/). Claim: under-five mortality was 5.2 per 1,000 live births in 2024, continuing a long decline from 21.6 in 1990; the page also lists infant mortality at 4 and neonatal mortality at 2. Locator/excerpt: lines 5146-5160 and 5331-5360 on the open page. Type/credibility: multilateral data portal; high credibility for the indicator values. Temporal fit: direct 2024 outcome. Attribution/limits: strong welfare signal, but mostly long-run baseline and not a 2024 policy-specific result. Contrary points: does not show service quality, access, or inequality. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`.

15. `N15` `IMF press briefing transcript` — IMF, 22 Feb 2024: [https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/22/tr022224-com-press-briefing-transcript](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/22/tr022224-com-press-briefing-transcript). Claim: the IMF said Russia was “in a war economy,” with heavy military expenditure and social transfers boosting consumption, but inflation was rising and the economy showed overheating; skilled labor losses were also harming medium-term prospects. Type/credibility: multilateral macro assessment; high credibility for the diagnosis. Temporal fit: direct 2024 assessment. Attribution/limits: negative for sustainability and human-capital pressure, but macro context is not the same as social-service delivery. Contrary points: the transcript does note consumption support from social transfers. Lenses: `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

16. `N16` `Bank of Russia raises the key rate to 18%` — Bank of Russia, 26 Jul 2024: [https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/pr/?file=26072024_133000Key_e.htm](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/pr/?file=26072024_133000Key_e.htm). Claim: the central bank raised the key rate to 18% because inflation and domestic demand were running above supply, with labor shortages and sanctions adding pressure. Type/credibility: primary monetary-policy record; high credibility. Temporal fit: direct 2024 policy response. Attribution/limits: this is not Putin personally, but it is part of the macro environment his government created and had to manage. Contrary points: tighter policy can stabilize prices but also constrains consumption and investment. Lenses: `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

17. `N17` `Reuters on Russia’s labor squeeze and wage growth` — Reuters, 5 Jun 2024, syndicated via Investing.com: [https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/soaring-wages-recordlow-unemployment-underscore-russias-labour-squeeze-3472155](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/soaring-wages-recordlow-unemployment-underscore-russias-labour-squeeze-3472155). Claim: real wages rose sharply and unemployment hit a record low, but Reuters said the growth was driven by defense spending and state-funded arms production, which masked weak living-standard improvements. Type/credibility: high-quality wire reporting, but accessed via syndication. Temporal fit: direct 2024 labor-market evidence. Attribution/limits: useful as an independent check on Rosstat, but still macro-level rather than ruler-specific social-service proof. Contrary points: it supports a narrow household-income improvement story while also showing war-driven distortion. Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`.

18. `N18` `World Bank Macro Poverty Outlook for Russian Federation` — World Bank, 3 Apr 2024: [https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099556304052484586](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099556304052484586). Claim: the World Bank projected growth of 2.2% in 2024 and a modest poverty decline through 2026, while noting that the outlook depended on loose fiscal policy and that predictable policy was needed. Type/credibility: multilateral country brief; high credibility. Temporal fit: 2024 forecast for the target year. Attribution/limits: this is forward-looking, so it is useful only as a contemporaneous assessment, not proof of eventual 2024 welfare results. Contrary points: the same brief flags weak medium-term prospects and the need for predictable policy. Lenses: `6B.5`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

**Search and rejection summary**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across `government.ru`, `kremlin.ru`, `rosstat.gov.ru`, `minzdrav.gov.ru`, `cbr.ru`, `imf.org`, `worldbank.org`, `data.worldbank.org`, `data.unicef.org`, and Reuters wire reproductions.
- I retained 18 URLs above and rejected the rest as follows:
- Duplicates: multiple Rosstat quarterly poverty releases were partly overlapping; I kept the ones that added distinct temporal slices (`Q1`, `Q3`, full-year/Q4, and inequality). Reuters stories syndicated across several platforms were collapsed to the cleanest available wire copy.
- Weak or too generic: global UNICEF annual reports, global HDR pages, broad World Bank poverty pages not Russia-specific, and generic country landing pages without 2024 Russia claims were not useful enough for ruler attribution.
- Blocked/timeout: some `government.ru` pages timed out on open, but the search-result snippets were sufficient where the policy text itself was the evidence. I did not rely on pages whose content could not be recovered.
- Out-of-period: 2025 or 2026 items were kept only when they explicitly reported 2024 outcomes or 2024-adjacent policy implementation. Otherwise they were excluded.
- Relevance pruning: I excluded sources that described general macro conditions without a welfare nexus, or social commentary without a traceable claim about Russian 2024 welfare policy or outcomes.

**Remaining gaps**
- The weakest part of the dossier is direct, independent evidence on service quality, not just coverage or spending. Education quality, rural access, disability inclusion, and mental-health or housing outcomes remain thinly evidenced.
- There is still limited independent evidence on how much of the income and poverty improvement was caused by Putin-era social policy versus war-economy wage pressure, labor shortages, and inflation.
- Regional and group-level distribution is only partly covered. I have one Rosstat inequality release, but not a strong subnational or vulnerable-group breakdown for 2024.
- If you want a tighter future judgment, more search on household surveys, regional health/education access, and disability/child welfare would help more than more macro articles.
